premise: When my sister was dying, I moved into her $380,000 condo, spent $88,000 of my widow’s savings on her experimental treatments, and was promised the condo in a notarized letter so her son couldn’t contest it; the day after the funeral my nephew produced a trust that left the condo to him and called my payments ‘rent.’ I found a voicemail where my sister told him he’d be cut off if he touched my inheritance, sued for unjust enrichment, and won a $195,000 judgment — when he couldn’t pay, I foreclosed on the condo, now rent it to traveling nurses, and deduct his garnished wages as ‘emotional damages’ on my tax return.
